title: Macroscopic atomically precise mechanosynthesis

concept.text: Macroscopic atomically precise mechanosynthesis would manufacture a handleable solid by using position-controlled chemical operations to place reactive fragments and direct their bonding throughout a prescribed three-dimensional structure. Atomic placement, composition and local bonding would become deliberate manufacturing choices. The target goes beyond drawing patterns on a surface: it requires repeated operations that extend construction into a volume while controlling errors.

Conceptual synthesis: the defining capability is controlled construction, rather than simply obtaining an orderly crystal. A convincing process would connect its sequence of positional chemical operations to the intended internal structure, including deliberately specified local features. It need not manipulate every atom separately if controlled fragment placement and bonding can reliably produce the prescribed result. The innovation remains hypothetical at macroscopic scale.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would make atomic structure throughout a manufactured solid a practical design variable. The supplied research reports surface-scale control of composition, bonding and spatial placement; extending such control through a handleable object would allow manufacturing decisions at a much finer structural level. Prescribed defects, interfaces and small mechanical structures are plausible applications, conditional on reliable construction and suitable designs.

Conditional impact synthesis: useful new materials would also require stability, suitable properties and performance under operating conditions. Precise construction alone would not guarantee strength, fatigue resistance, low friction or economical production. The analogy to programmable manufacturing has limits: chemical reactions, tool access, competing reaction pathways and material stability constrain what can be built. Mechanical self-replicating factories are a further possibility requiring extensive additional capabilities, not an automatic consequence of atomic placement.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target is error-controlled, three-dimensional positional chemistry at a useful scale and rate. The supplied paper identifies reliable scanning-probe synthesis using out-of-plane bonds to build extended structures as a continuing challenge. Its stated foundation is reliable placement of reactive fragments at predetermined sites, followed by iterative chemical operations on the resulting structures. Turning those operations into sustained construction throughout a growing solid is the central missing capability in this evidence base.

The reported experiment uses prepared hydrogenated silicon surfaces, molecular tool changes and operation at 4 K, and it includes off-target outcomes. These details expose concrete demands on reaction selectivity, tool preparation and handling, and the ability to continue construction after each operation. Cryogenic operation is an operating condition of this demonstration. The evidence does not show that warmer operation is necessary for success, or that temperature is a universal obstacle to mechanosynthesis.

Engineering synthesis: scaling would require maintaining tool access to construction sites, supplying reactive fragments, preserving positional control as the object grows, and detecting, preventing or correcting defects before they compromise later steps. Throughput, tool lifetime, yield and process stability would have to support a useful manufacturing rate. These are inferred requirements for the proposed capability, not experimentally established impossibility results. The supplied evidence does not resolve whether a scalable architecture can meet them together.

current_state.text: Cowie, Deimert, Groome and colleagues’ 2026 preprint, “Atomically precise mechanosynthesis of carbon structures on hydrogenated Si(100) by inverted-mode STM,” reports donation of C₂ units from surface-deposited molecules to pre-patterned reactive sites on hydrogen-passivated Si(100). The supplied review describes operation at 4 K, repeated surface patterning and extension to structures assigned as containing four carbon atoms. These are relevant demonstrations of controlled atomic-scale chemical operations on a prepared surface; they do not demonstrate a macroscopic bulk manufacturing process.

The reported structural assignments draw on imaging, simulations and exclusion of alternative interpretations. The supplied review supports describing what the authors report, but does not independently validate those assignments. Its available material included the main article and captions; supplementary material was absent, and figure images were not supplied for inspection. Those limitations constrain independent experimental and visual verification without establishing that the reported results are false.

The retained report is a preprint, and no peer-reviewed DOI was verified in the supplied research. Its arXiv v1 masthead gives 26 May 2026, while the manuscript text bears an August 24, 2026 date; the precise version chronology remains unclear. The supplied freshness search record is empty, so it cannot establish whether later work superseded this report or comprehensively determine the field’s status as of 1 November 2026. The evidence supports a surface-scale foundation while leaving macroscopic feasibility unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: build a freestanding covalent specimen at least 1 mm in each dimension through positional chemistry, with a prescribed three-dimensional internal structure. The millimetre threshold is an author-selected benchmark for a handleable bulk object, not a documented consensus standard. The demonstration should show how controlled placement and iterative bonding created the intended volume, and distinguish that contribution from conventional crystal growth or assembly of previously fabricated components.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification: independently quantify placement or bonding errors across representative regions of the specimen’s volume, with a stated sampling plan, measurement sensitivity and statistical confidence. Diffraction could establish average crystal structure, but would not by itself verify every intended bond or local defect. Complementary local measurements should test the deliberately prescribed features. Sampled measurements can establish demonstrated accuracy and breadth; they cannot certify every bond throughout the object or prove literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed verification

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: define acceptable error rates, yield and a useful build-rate target before the trial, then report build time, tool changes, defect detection and correction, operating conditions and failed builds. Merely reporting these quantities would not establish useful performance. Repeated builds and independent replication should test whether the result is reproducible. The demonstrated scope should identify supported materials, geometries, interfaces and limits on construction access, without extrapolating a successful specimen to arbitrary structures.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: MEC-07, “Bulk structural solids at a large fraction of ideal strength,” and MEC-04, “Ambient fatigue immunity in bulk structural metals,” concern material performance. Mechanosynthesis might offer control over defects or interfaces relevant to those goals, but precise fabrication would not establish either strength or fatigue immunity. MEC-05, “Programmable solids that become different load-bearing mechanisms,” concerns changes in mechanical configuration or behavior; atomically precise fabrication could support particular designs, while remaining a distinct manufacturing capability.

Roster-based synthesis: MEC-09, “Mechanical self-replication of a production cell from feedstock,” requires an entire production system to reproduce its necessary components and functions. MEC-06 could potentially contribute a fabrication process, but does not supply that system capability. MEC-13, “General-purpose synthesis of practical mechanisms,” concerns generating practical mechanism designs; MEC-06 concerns making prescribed structures. MEC-10, “Stress-directed growth of load-bearing structures,” overlaps in constructing three-dimensional objects, but its organizing principle is growth directed by stress rather than positional control of atomic chemistry.

Roster-based synthesis: MEC-02, “Service-life superlubricity in ordinary machine contacts,” MEC-11, “Transferable prediction of wear and component life,” and MEC-12, “Predictive mechanics of real, evolving surface contacts,” share concerns about surfaces, defects and changing interfaces. Atomically precise specimens could provide controlled experimental structures for these problems. They would not by themselves establish persistent low friction or predictive models of contacts and wear, especially as surfaces evolve during service.

Roster-based synthesis: MEC-08, “Distributed actuators that simultaneously match skeletal muscle,” and MEC-14, “Low-cost mechanical storage with high efficiency over long periods,” could potentially use specially fabricated materials or small mechanical structures. Their completion depends on system performance, durability and practical cost beyond manufacturing precision. MEC-03, “Engines that make sub-100 °C heat worth converting,” likewise concerns useful conversion performance; atomically precise construction would not itself resolve that objective.

Roster-based synthesis: MEC-01, “An engineering-predictive theory of turbulent flow,” has no direct enabling relationship established by the supplied evidence. It concerns predictive theory, while MEC-06 concerns a manufacturing process. Across disciplines, MEC-06 sits at the intersection of mechanical engineering’s positioning, tooling and process control with surface chemistry, materials science, microscopy and atomic-scale electronics.

change_log.change: Preserved MEC-06 and its title, while expanding the explanation of positional chemistry, iterative bonding and construction throughout a volume.
change_log.reason: The innovation is macroscopic controlled fabrication; the supplied surface experiment is a foundation rather than completion of that concept.

change_log.change: Bound statements about the missing capability to the supplied evidence rather than asserting a comprehensive field-wide absence as of November 2026.
change_log.reason: The review had no freshness search record capable of resolving the broader state of the field.

change_log.change: Added the reported 4 K operating condition, molecular tool changes, off-target outcomes, repeated patterning and assigned four-carbon structures.
change_log.reason: These details clarify both the demonstrated achievement and the concrete demands of scaling.

change_log.change: Reframed temperature as a demonstrated operating condition and scaling requirements as engineering inferences.
change_log.reason: The evidence does not establish that warmer operation is necessary or that the identified barriers are universal impossibility results.

change_log.change: Preserved preprint status, uncertain version chronology and the limits of structural verification.

change_log.change: Separated direct manufacturing consequences from conditional materials applications and self-replicating factories.
change_log.reason: Useful performance and self-replication require additional designs and capabilities beyond precise placement.

change_log.change: Retained the proposed 1 mm specimen and strengthened verification and reproducibility criteria without inventing numerical performance thresholds.
change_log.reason: The size is a proposed benchmark; acceptable errors and build rates remain unspecified, and representative measurements cannot certify every bond.

unresolved_issues: Whether later research or peer-reviewed publication changes the assessment is unresolved because the supplied freshness search record is empty.
The relationship between the 26 May 2026 arXiv v1 masthead and the August 24, 2026 manuscript date remains unclear.
The reported structural assignments have not been independently validated here; supplementary material and figure images were unavailable to the supplied review.
A scalable architecture for sustained construction beyond surface-bound structures, with practical throughput, tool handling and defect management, remains unestablished by the supplied evidence.
Acceptable error rates, sampling confidence, yield and useful build-rate thresholds require application-specific definition; no numerical resolutions were supplied.
The proposed 1 mm benchmark is not a documented consensus criterion, and feasibility across different materials and geometries remains open.
